title: Reduce embedding endpoint tail latency via adaptive micro-batching and kernel tuning
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The embeddings endpoint shows unacceptable tail latency for medium-to-high concurrency workloads. Baseline: API p50 ~45ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~650ms under synthetic burst tests (1-2k RPS per node). This is causing occasional downstream query timeouts and elevation in error budgets for several customers.

Goal: Reduce tail latency (p99) to <200ms and p95 <80ms for 95% of steady-state workload shapes while preserving or improving end-to-end throughput (target >=300 req/s per GPU for the 2.7B embedding model). Maintain functional parity and no regression in result quality.

Scope: Focus on server-side runtime changes (micro-batching scheduling, kernel selection/tuning, quantization path adjustments) and observability (tail-span tracing, per-request queue metrics). Exclude client-side SDK changes and model architecture changes.

Approach:
- Implement adaptive micro-batching scheduler that groups requests by arrival time and request size (embedding length) with a dynamic time window (1-6ms) and max micro-batch size (2-16). Prioritize low-latency tokens by offering a fast-path when queue depth == 0.
- Add kernel tuning knobs exposed to runtime: fused matmul+gelu, packed KV cache fetch paths, int8 quantized kernels for common dims, and reduce kernel launch overhead via pre-warmed CUDA streams.
- Introduce per-request tracing IDs, queueing latency histograms, and flamegraph export to identify hot paths contributing to tail.
- Run controlled chaos and burst tests with realistic request distributions (short/long vectors, small/big concurrency) and compare against baseline.

Success deliverables: PRs merged to runtime repo, Grafana panels showing p50/p95/p99 improvements, a postmortem-style doc summarizing trade-offs, and a canary rollout plan for runtime-2.3.

Constraints & trade-offs: Micro-batching improves throughput at the cost of small added latency; adaptive logic must never increase average latency for low-traffic customers. Some kernel optimizations (int8) may affect numerical parity; we will gate those behind compatibility flags and run regression evals against the embeddings reference set.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings endpoint <= 200ms in controlled burst tests (same test harness as baseline)
p95 <= 80ms and p50 <= 60ms across representative workloads
No accuracy regression on embeddings reference set (cosine similarity deviation <= 0.5% on average)
Runtime changes merged and feature-flagged with a canary plan and rollout playbook
Grafana dashboards updated with queueing latency, micro-batch size distribution, and kernel selection breakdown

comments: 2026-02-26 — Ava Martinez: Kicked off spike to capture queueing traces. Initial flamegraphs point to two hotspots: kernel launch overhead and small-batch cuBLAS inefficiency.

2026-03-02 — Ravi Singh: Prototype micro-batcher implemented. Early results: p95 reduced by ~30% on small bursts (from 180ms -> 125ms) but p99 still at ~420ms due to outliers when kernel fallback occurs.
2026-03-05 — Priya Nair (design review): Approved scheduler UX; requested telemetry for micro-batch size distribution and request-size bucketing.
2026-03-09 — Mandeep Rao: Added fused matmul+activation kernel and pre-warmed streams. In A/B test, p99 improved to ~220ms on the 2.7B embedding model when micro-batch window tuned to 3ms.

2026-03-11 — Perf Team: Identified one reproducible tail case where queueing from long-running concurrent priority requests causes >300ms spikes. Proposed mitigation: bounded preemption and request admission control.
2026-03-12 — Ravi Singh: Opened PR #2048 for micro-batcher and instrumentation. Added canary config and metric names. Need SRE signoff on rollback hooks.
2026-03-13 — SRE (Danielle): Reviewed canary; requested a playbook entry for disk/GPU contention scenario and a dashboard alert for micro-batch queue length > 50
